title: Changing, Adding, and Removing Elements
objective: Update a list in place by assigning to an index, adding items with append() and insert(), and removing items with del, pop(), and remove().

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Lists are mutable, meaning you can change their contents after creating them. To replace an item, assign a new value to its index: supplies[0] = "reinforced tent" swaps out whatever used to be at position 0.
To grow a list, use .append(item) to add something to the end, or .insert(index, item) to slide something into a specific position, pushing every later item back by one.

To shrink a list, you have three tools. del list_name[index] removes whatever is at that position and forgets its value entirely. .pop() removes and returns the last item (or .pop(index) for a specific position), so you can still use the value after removing it. .remove(value) searches for the first item that matches value and deletes it — use this when you know what the item is but not where it lives.
explanation.rule: Assign to an index to replace an item, append()/insert() to add one, and del/pop()/remove() to take one away — pop() is the only one that hands the removed value back to you.

examples.title: Editing a Loadout
examples.code:
loadout = ["sword", "shield", "potion"]
loadout[1] = "tower shield"
loadout.append("map")
loadout.insert(0, "torch")
print(loadout)
examples.note: The index assignment swaps 'shield' out, append() adds to the end, and insert(0, ...) pushes everything else one spot to the right.

examples.title: Three Ways to Remove
examples.code:
crates = ["rope", "nails", "canteen", "nails"]
del crates[0]
last = crates.pop()
crates.remove("nails")
print(crates)
print(last)
examples.note: del crates[0] discards the first item outright. pop() removes the last item and returns it into 'last'. remove('nails') deletes only the first matching 'nails' it finds.

checks.question: You know an item's exact value but not its index. Which method should you use to delete it?

feedback.correct: Correct — .remove(value) searches the list for a matching value and deletes the first one it finds.
feedback.incorrect: Think about which method searches by value instead of by position.

checks.question: What makes .pop() different from del?
options: pop() only works on the first item
pop() returns the removed value so you can use it

feedback.correct: Correct — pop() hands back the value it removed; del just deletes it.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. One of these gives you the removed value back.

assignment.title: Camp Supply List
assignment.brief: Write update_supplies(supplies) that edits a supply list step by step: upgrade the first item, add a new item, insert an urgent item, remove one item by value, and remove the last item.
requirements: Replace the first item (index 0) with "reinforced tent".
Use .pop() to remove the last item.
assignment.starterCode:
def update_supplies(supplies):
    # Modify supplies step by step, then print the result.
    pass

update_supplies(["tent", "rope", "canteen"])
assignment.solutionCode:
def update_supplies(supplies):
    supplies[0] = "reinforced tent"
    supplies.append("extra rations")
    supplies.insert(1, "torch")
    supplies.remove("rope")
    supplies.pop()
    print(supplies)

update_supplies(["tent", "rope", "canteen"])
assignment.testHarness:
# ---- Code Forge validation ----
import io, contextlib
_cf_buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(_cf_buf):

_cf_result = _cf_buf.getvalue()
print("__CF_TEST_OUTPUT__")

assignment.outputCheckLabel: update_supplies(["tent", "rope", "canteen"]) prints the final supply list

hints: Start by assigning directly to supplies[0] to replace the first item.
supplies.append(...) always adds to the end; supplies.insert(1, ...) squeezes an item in at position 1.
supplies.remove("rope") searches for the value "rope" and deletes it — you don't need to know its index.
supplies.pop() with no argument removes whatever is currently last, which by that point is the item you appended.
Do the steps in order: replace, append, insert, remove, pop, then print.
